text: A strange chill, whether it was the chill of the room or of their own bodies, now began to creep gradually over them all. <break time="0.8s" /> The doctor took up the rose of half a century, and they saw with dismay that its fresh petals were already shriveling until it became as dry and fragile as before. <break time="0.8s" /> Looking at one another, they shuddered, for they saw that the deep furrows of age were returning and that each of them was once again an old, withered person. <break time="0.8s" /> Are we grown old again, so soon, cried they, dolefully, and indeed the Water of Youth possessed merely a virtue more transient than that of wine. <break time="0.8s" /> Yes, friends, ye are old again, said Doctor Heidegger, and, lo, the Water of Youth is all lavished on the ground, but I do not lament it. <break time="0.8s" /> For if the fountain gushed at my very doorstep, I would not stoop to bathe my lips in it, no, though its delirium were for years instead of moments. <break time="0.8s" /> Such is the lesson ye have taught me. <break time="0.8s" /> But the doctors four friends had taught no such lesson to themselves. <break time="0.8s" /> They resolved forthwith to make a pilgrimage to Florida, and there to drink at morning, noon, and night from the Fountain of Youth.
